methodBriefing.what: Study one accurate model, explain each rule in your own words, repair any gap, then explain it again without copying.

Compare your explanation with the model and fix what is missing or unclear.
Explain it again more clearly and more briefly.

activities.title: Product rule model
activities.body: Study the rule and its structure. Then do the check that follows.

essentialIdeas: Differentiate a product by using the product rule: the derivative of the first factor times the second, plus the first factor times the derivative of the second.

activities.label: product-rule-recall
activities.title: Explain the product rule
activities.body: Write the rule in your own words. Keep it short and exact.
activities.concept: Product rule
activities.correctAnswer: Differentiate a product by taking the derivative of the first factor times the second, then add the first factor times the derivative of the second.
activities.feedback: A complete answer names both terms in the sum and shows that both factors matter. A common gap is differentiating only one factor.

activities.label: chain-rule-model
activities.title: Chain rule model
activities.body: Study the rule and its structure. Then do the check that follows.

essentialIdeas: Differentiate a composite function by using the chain rule: differentiate the outside function, then multiply by the derivative of the inside function.

activities.label: chain-rule-fix
activities.title: Fix the chain rule step
activities.body: Correct the rule in one sentence. Then give the key step.
activities.concept: Chain rule
activities.correctAnswer: Differentiate the outside function first, then multiply by the derivative of the inside function.
activities.feedback: A complete repair keeps both parts of the composite function connected. A common gap is differentiating the outside part but forgetting the inside derivative.

activities.label: chain-rule-restate
activities.title: Explain the chain rule again
activities.body: Restate the rule from memory in plain language. Do not copy the model.
activities.concept: Chain rule
activities.correctAnswer: For a composite function, differentiate the outside function and multiply by the derivative of the inside function.
activities.feedback: A strong restatement keeps the outside and inside roles clear. If you mention only one layer, the explanation is still incomplete.

activities.label: product-rule-check
activities.title: Product rule check
activities.body: Choose the rule that fits this derivative. Then answer on your own.
activities.concept: Product rule
choices: Use the product rule: differentiate each factor in turn and add the results.
Use the chain rule because one factor is inside the other.
Use only the power rule on the first factor.
Use only the derivative of the second factor.
activities.correctAnswer: Use the product rule: differentiate each factor in turn and add the results.
activities.feedback: A product of functions needs two derivative terms. The chain rule is for a composite function, not a product.
